threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers—they're the ones standing at the bus stop, confused, staring at the timetable like it's ancient hieroglyphs.
Caught the N37 last night; a group of art students turned the back seat into a makeshift sketch class. Hilarious to watch their chaotic creativity unfold.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy walking his pet ferret on a leash outside Spätkauf, I realized Neukölln truly has its own vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you stumble across a park where neighbors gather to swap books and pastries like they’re at a potluck. It’s the little communal acts that feel so uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: When you know that Muni delays are the urban version of a casual coffee break, you’re definitely from here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just witnessed a guy in a full tuxedo hop off a delayed bus, grab a slice from that corner pizza joint, and sprint to an event. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just a trendy photo spot, but it’s really the daily life of families packed into narrow streets, not just nightlife.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll see them standing confused at the metro ticket machines, ignoring the ‘T-10’ posters, and trying to pay for a single ride with cash.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still use the bus to get to Dalston; real locals know to swap to the Overground instead for quicker connections.
Last night on the 36, I saw a guy serenading a pigeon with a ukulele. The bird just looked confused, but everyone else loved it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard the spontaneous jam session in the park, a bunch of kids dancing, and someone selling homemade baklava—it hit me hard.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Döner stand disguised as a library. Grab a kebab and a book, then sit by the canal. Unreal!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate BART delays; they’ve got a backup bus route memorized and don’t even flinch at a Civic Center evacuation.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a conductor over the loudspeakers asking riders to be patient while a dog took its sweet time crossing the tracks. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists love taking photos of the streets but miss the little pots of herbs outside locals' doors—it's like our secret neighborhood spice rack.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the metro ticket machines—it's like watching a deer in headlights. Classic sign.
